title: The `sync` package: `Mutex`, `RWMutex` and when a channel is worse

videos.script: Lesson 1 left you with a counter and five wrong totals. This lesson fixes it with a lock. {{mutex}} A mutex lets one goroutine at a time into a few lines of code. Put one around the increment, and the total is right every time. Then a struct with a mutex inside, and one wrong receiver. Four hundred thousand calls, and a total of zero. go vet names the mistake in one line. {{rw}} Next, a lock for data that is mostly read. Many readers at once, one writer alone. With real work under the lock it is three times faster. With almost none, it is slower. {{three}} Last, the same counter three ways. A mutex, an atomic number, and a goroutine that owns the number behind a channel. The channel is the slowest and the longest to read. {{close}} Lesson 9 finishes the sync package: waiting, doing something once, and a concurrent map.
